findings.title: Legacy writes can erase progress already acknowledged by the new app
findings.problem: Accepting an update that omits revision and merely incrementing the counter does not protect its blob from being stale. The pre-change client writes whole snapshots without revision checks. This trigger accepts those snapshots even after another client has saved additional answers. Advancing revision records the overwrite; it does not preserve the overwritten progress.
findings.failure_scenario: An old tab holds 30 answers. A new tab saves answer 31 and receives a successful acknowledgement. The old tab then answers another question or changes a setting and autosaves its older snapshot. The trigger accepts that blob, removing answer 31. Reloading the new tab loses the answer and its associated progress.
findings.fix: Prevent revision-less clients from replacing newer progress, for example by requiring them to reload before further writes, or implement a server-side compatibility merge that preserves existing answers and their effects. Test the actual legacy upsert against the database after a newer-client save; testing revision increments alone does not cover this loss.

findings.title: An invalidated load is returned as an empty account and can enable destructive autosaving
findings.problem: store.get returns null when accountEpoch changes during getSession. readProgress interprets null as a confirmed absence of saved progress, and loadProgress has no cancellation or load-generation check. The shipped React.StrictMode development entry reproduces this: its effect cleanup calls store.releaseAccount(), invalidating the first read, but that read continues through the new-account path and sets loaded=true. If the replacement read fails, it sets only loadState, leaving autosave enabled.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the app through app-main.jsx in development with real saved progress and delay or fail the replacement progress SELECT. StrictMode's first, invalidated load resolves as null and enables autosave using defaults while the authoritative read is still pending or has failed. For a legacy row at revision 0, writeAt(0, defaults) can directly replace the saved blob despite the displayed read-error state.
findings.fix: Represent invalidated reads as cancellation, never as no-row results. Give each load a generation/cancellation guard and allow only the current successful load to apply state or enable saving. Also explicitly disable saving on load failure. Add a browser regression mounting the real entry under StrictMode with a delayed or failed authoritative SELECT.

findings.title: Conflict reconciliation discards ability updates from actual legacy answers
findings.problem: replayUnseen sends newly discovered legacy rows through applyAnswer without a source or canonical key. applyAnswer classifies those rows as unclassified and deliberately makes no ability update. When the merged log also contains a new attempt-bearing answer, reconcileProgress installs replayed.ability, discarding the legacy client's ability delta. The regression named "keeps the ability update from an answer the older app saved without an attempt id" does not exercise the old format: it creates a current applyAnswer row and removes attempt and seq, but retains source and key, which the pre-change record function never wrote.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tabs share a baseline. The old client saves a correct Pharmacology answer as {id, cat, diff, correct} and advances Pharmacology ability. The new client saves a Management of Care answer with an attempt ID and encounters the revision conflict. Reconciliation preserves both log rows but replays only the new client's ability effect; Pharmacology theta and n revert to the baseline, producing an incorrect readiness estimate.
findings.fix: Handle genuinely unscoped legacy additions without dropping the ability changes already computed for them, or refuse the incompatible merge rather than reporting success with corrupted maths. Replace the legacy regression fixture with the exact pre-change row shape—no source, key, attempt, timestamp, or rating—and assert both categories' resulting ability and readiness.

assessment: Do not release yet. The warfarin correction is appropriate, and the supplied images introduce no apparent clinical errors. However, the persistence changes still contain paths that can erase saved answers or corrupt ability estimates. This review is based on the supplied code; tests and builds were not executed.
